stem.text: The mechanism for the reaction between ethanal and hydrogen cyanide starts with the step shown.

stem.alt: Ethanal (CH3CHO) with curved arrows: the lone pair on the cyanide ion (CN-) attacks the carbonyl carbon, and the C=O pi bond moves onto the oxygen.

stem.text: What is the correct structure of the intermediate ion formed, and what is the next step in this mechanism?

A.alt: CH3CH(CN)O+ with a C=N double bond to N and a curved arrow from the H-CN bond to the oxygen.

B.alt: CH3CH(CN)O- with lone pairs on O and a C=N double bond; curved arrows from the O- lone pair to H of H-CN and from the H-CN bond to CN.

C.alt: CH3CH(CN)O+ with a C≡N triple bond and a curved arrow from the H-CN bond to the oxygen.

D.alt: CH3CH(CN)O- with lone pairs on O and a C≡N triple bond; curved arrows from the O- lone pair to H of H-CN and from the H-CN bond to CN.
